baselineAssumptions.description: The authors assume a baseline of unmanaged grasslands before the introduction of grazing and fire management practices.

frames.description: A frame focusing on the ecological consequences of grazing and fire.
frames.evidenceSnippet: The effects of livestock grazing (Pillar et al., 2005) and frequent burning (Souza Castilhos & Jacques, 2017) on native grasslands are well documented.
frames.label: ecological impact of management practices

declaredActions.statement: Sustainable land management practices should be implemented to preserve biodiversity.

declaredProblems.statement: Native grasslands are threatened by management practices such as grazing and fire.

expectedEffects.statement: Implementing sustainable management can maintain or restore native grassland ecosystems.

observedStatements: grazing and fire impact native grasslands
possibleReadings: the authors emphasize the need for sustainable land management
management practices can lead to both positive and negative outcomes depending on implementation

trajectoryAnalogies.analogy: The analogy with other disturbed ecosystems, such as agricultural landscapes (Zapata T., 2019), is drawn to support the findings.
trajectoryAnalogies.justification: To demonstrate that the impacts observed in this study are not unique and can be seen in similar systems.
